name: Termite Mound
description: Collective climate engineering intelligence achieving zero-energy temperature control through passive convective chimney design. Maintains fungal agriculture at precisely 23C through adjustable ventilation openings. Stigmergic construction coordination — no central plan, no architect, yet the resulting structures are aerodynamically optimized. Compression arch geometry distributes structural loads across the colony, scaling with population.

core_attributes.pattern: passive climate control, fungal agriculture, stigmergic architecture

scope.definition: CO2 concentration regulation precision inside Macrotermes mound — deviation from target 2.7% CO2 during peak metabolic activity (hot midday), maintained by passive convective ventilation.

evidence.source: Turner (2000) 'Architecture and morphogenesis in the mound of Macrotermes michaelseni', Cimbebasia 16:143-175; Korb & Linsenmair (1999) 'The architecture of termite mounds', Behavioral Ecology.
cross_domain_examples: Macrotermes mound maintains 2.5-2.9% CO2 vs external 0.04% across 30°C temperature range
convective ventilation driven by metabolic heat of fungus garden — no active pumping required
Eastgate Centre building (Zimbabwe): passive ventilation inspired by termite mound convection — 90% energy savings vs conventional HVAC

scope.falsifiability: If CO2 measurements inside sealed mound sections show concentration excursions above 5% during normal conditions, the passive convective regulation model is insufficient.
scope.measurement_limits: Regulation precision is mound-age and architecture-dependent. Young mounds with incomplete conduit networks show larger CO2 fluctuations. Measurement requires CO2 sensors embedded without disrupting convection.

scope.definition: Structural precision of termite pillar and arch formation — fraction of pillars reaching optimal load-bearing diameter (relative to arch span) without any central control or blueprint.

evidence.source: Bonabeau et al. (1997) 'Self-organization in social insects', Trends in Ecology & Evolution 12:188-193; Theraulaz & Bonabeau (1995) 'Modelling the collective building of complex architectures by social insects',
cross_domain_examples: Nasutitermes pillar spacing approximates Euler beam buckling formula optimum within 12%
termite arch formation emerges from pheromone-gradient building without explicit coordination
slime mold network formation: analogous stigmergic optimization of tube network topology
ant colony tunnel branching: same pheromone-gradient construction principle at smaller scale

scope.falsifiability: If artificially disrupted pheromone gradients (via chemical masking) result in structurally equivalent constructions, pheromone-based stigmergy is not the building guide.
scope.measurement_limits: Construction precision decreases in heterogeneous substrate where pheromone diffusion is disrupted. Pillar diameter precision is climate-dependent — humidity affects both pheromone diffusion and material curing.

scope.definition: Nitrogen conversion efficiency of termite fungal garden — fraction of plant cellulose substrate nitrogen made bioavailable to termites via Termitomyces fungal enzymatic processing.

evidence.source: Nobre et al. (2010) 'Farming termites determine the genetic make-up of the fungal comb', Journal of Evolutionary Biology 23:1789-1796; Poulsen et al. (2014) termite-fungus mutualism efficiency.
cross_domain_examples: Termitomyces decompose lignocellulose releasing 0.88-0.93 of bound nitrogen for termite absorption
leaf-cutter ant fungal gardens: convergent agricultural mutualism with Leucoagaricus achieving 0.85 efficiency
human cheese and bread fermentation: microorganism-mediated nutrient liberation from plant substrates

scope.falsifiability: If termites without their Termitomyces fungal comb show equivalent or greater body nitrogen content than mound-dwelling termites, the agricultural mutualism provides no nutritional advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Conversion efficiency is substrate quality-dependent — dry woody material (poor substrate) reduces efficiency to 0.70-0.75. Measurement requires N-15 isotope tracing through the cellulose-to-termite pathway.
